The drive agent is a leaf subagent with no Agent tool, and /converge works only by dispatching drivers, hunters, fixers and verifiers through the task drain, so a leaf cannot run it. Running it in this session would also edit the tree that the sprint certification run is checking. Checked what a consumer receives instead: converge core in a mktemp+git init scratch project installed .claude/skills/converge, the four agent profiles, .ok-planner/bin/review and tasks, and seeded .ok-planner/review/{config.json,project.md,catalog/accept.md}. The review CLI steps run there (review files listed app/divide.py; review areas wrote 2 areas), but the steps that find or fix refuse outside a run /converge starts. The CLI is the orchestrator's mechanics, not a surface the story is offered through.; the story promises: defects across the product found and fixed without the owner, who meets only the questions that need judgment; saw: could not run the loop from a leaf drive agent; evidence: 'review hunts --areas areas.json --out hunts.json --first' -> 'review: tasks item list --pool merges --key gate --json failed: tasks: no run selected: run `tasks init` or `tasks use`, or set OK_TASKS' exit=1; 'review stories' in a fresh consumer -> 'review: cannot list .ok-planner/design/stories: [Errno 2] No such file or directory' exit=1

body: Tried to run /converge sprint <path> on a scratch sprint in a scratch consumer project (mktemp -d, git init, converge core). The slash command is an orchestrating ceremony: it files a review task on the ok-review forking profile, forks pass agents, and dispatches fixers and verifiers. A leaf driver may not spawn subagents, so it cannot run the ceremony end to end. The run that dispatched this drive (converge-2026-10-04T060800: t1 review, t3-t14 drives) is itself a live /converge sprint run, but it had not reached its report when this driver closed. The story promises: when a sprint closes, the owner knows whether what they approved was delivered, and done means the same thing for every sprint. Saw: the user-visible guidance is uniform. .claude/rules/ok-planner-cheatsheet.md, .claude/rules/ok-cheatsheet.md, and .ok-planner/CLAUDE.md (Executing a sprint) all name /converge sprint <path> as the closing step of every sprint. The verdict itself comes only from the ceremony's agents and could not be observed. Evidence: the drive prompt says 'You are a leaf agent: never spawn subagents'; tasks status for the live run shows 'open t1 task review key=gate state=running'.

In a scratch consumer project (converge core, then git commit as base): wrote a minimal sprint at .ok-planner/sprints/2026-10-04-certify-completion-873314a4.md with a work item, implementation notes, a completion contract, and a closing /converge sprint line. Added src/app.py. Ran review changed --sprint S, which printed 'added src/app.py'. Ran tasks init, then review checks --base HEAD --sprint S, which filed exec t1 'node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline src/app.py'. Ran tasks next and tasks exec t1, which printed 'closed t1 done (exit 0)'. Ran review prompt --name sprint-review, which wrote the review agent's prompt. Committed the work, then ran review changed --sprint S again with no --base: it printed nothing and exited 0. The same happened with a recorded base file beside the sprint under the names <sprint>-base, <sprint>-base.txt, and <sprint>.base: none was honoured. Only an explicit --base HEAD~1 listed the change again ('added src/app.py'). The story promises: the owner knows, when a sprint closes, whether what they approved was delivered, the same way for every sprint. Saw: the command line runs the mechanical steps but gives no verdict on delivery. review --help and every subcommand's --help print bare usage with no description of what a step does, so an owner cannot tell from the command line which steps make a certification. review changed --sprint without --base falls back silently to HEAD. After the sprint's work is committed, that fallback reports an empty change with exit 0 and no warning that no base was recorded, so a review fed from it would see nothing to judge. Evidence: '== changed --sprint (no base file, work committed)' followed by no output and 'exit 0'; 'review changed --base HEAD~1 --sprint S' prints 'added src/app.py'; 'review changed --help' prints only 'usage: review changed [-h] [--base BASE] [--sprint SPRINT]'.

Noticed while driving certify-completion; this is outside that story. Ran plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/converge --help from the ok-plugins repo root to learn its modes. The core accepted --help as the no-mode converge and converged the repo root: it printed 'materialized: 74 files under .ok-planner/ and .claude/ (v23.0.0)' and 'Converged ok-planner at /Users/patrick/Documents/projects/research/ok-plugins', exit 0. The repo's vendored layer now shows unstaged rewrites, files stamped 06:09:38 (for example .claude/skills/converge/SKILL.md and .claude/agents/ok-opus.md; .claude/agents/ok-sonnet.md and several skill folders deleted). project.md reserves that rewrite for /ok as an owner act. Note that the session's skill listing had already changed just before this call, so another process may also have converged the root; this driver ran no git restore. Reproduced in a scratch repo: --help, -h, help, --version, and bogus each run a full converge and exit 0. A help flag or an unknown mode should be refused before anything is written. body: Commitment contradicted. decision:per-project-pinning, amended by this sprint, now says: 'Exactly one class legitimately runs from the payload: the administration process itself — diagnosis, bootstrap, and converge'. The base read 'Exactly two classes ... and read-only advisory verbs'; the sprint retired the advisory plumbline verbs and dropped the audit's payload fallback (B107). docs/integration-contract.md, rewritten by work item 18, still says in its 'Support scripts' section: 'Exactly two classes legitimately run from the carried payload: the administration process itself (...), and read-only advisory verbs falling back with an announcement in their output.' The normative contract permits a payload-run class the amended decision forbids and no payload verb uses. Scope: caused — the sentence was carried into the rewritten section while the decision it restates changed in the same sprint.

WI4 folds the plumbline audit contribution into one /audit skill. skills/audit/SKILL.md Requires: 'Without a design corpus ... run the coverage reading and the lint sweep alone, skipping the surface, the story and assumption tracks, and the reading of decisions and concepts.' Yet the spine's step 4 Enumerate still gates on showing the owner the /goal line naming .claude/skills/audit/goal.md for every a la carte run, and that goal's rule requires terms 1 (surface intent exists), 3 (assumption records exist) and 4 (extraction.json exists, produced by this run's extractor), and lists 'the surface intent missing; ... the extraction absent' under Not met. Trigger: /audit in a project with subjects and no .ok-planner/design/ (the common case B7 now creates: a plumbline-only project converged into the planner estate). Path: audit/SKILL.md::Requires -> skip surface -> Enumerate shows goal line -> goal checker reads goal.md::The goal rule. Harm: the goal checker reports the run not met for a run that did everything the skill prescribes, so a /goal-driven run never ends or reports false failure. Scope: caused by the change (the base planner goal applied only where the planner contribution ran; the no-design coverage-only path is new in the folded skill).

B6 ruling: 'migrate: the /ok report names the new rules and the lint_checks switch, the hook stays behind consent, and without node nothing is wired'. A project that ran ok-planner alone gains .claude/rules/plumbline-cheatsheet.md, plumbline-coding.md, the lint, and a lint that now runs on every consented edit (post-edit.js dropped its PLUMBLINE_MARKERS gate). Nothing tells the owner: plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md step 7's report template names only the version row, wiring, offers, migrations, and removed verbs; lint_checks appears there only in the retired budget row (line 96), which prints only when a /budget skill was removed. A planner-only owner learns neither that the comment/test rules now bind nor how to turn them off. Scope: caused by the change (B6 is this sprint's ruling).

B19/B21/B28/B29/B118 rule the retired-verb removal for copies of verbs the suite vendored: stamped files removed, project files offered. This sprint adds generic names to RETIRED_VENDORED (budget, events, explain, patterns, port, starter, suggest, version, open, close, slug, ci, plus ok-workspaces, ok-planner, execute-tasks), and retirements() treats any folder at those names whose SKILL.md lacks a suite stamp as 'the project's own whole' (out.append((name, [], files))), so offers() emits retired-verb:.claude/skills/<name> with What '.claude/skills/<name>/ holds files the project wrote at a name the suite retired; the vendored skills replace it' and Recommended: accept, whose fix git-rm's every file. Boundary user not ruled: a project the suite never vendored that verb into (a planner-only project at the base, which never ran the plumbline or workspaces core) that keeps its own unrelated skill at .claude/skills/close/, open/, version/, ci/, events/, or port/. Before (base core 9c7aff7: RETIRED_VENDORED held only suite-specific names like certify-work, verify-issues, converge-local), /ok left such a folder alone. After: /ok reports it as a retired suite verb that the vendored skills replace (not so: no vendored skill replaces the project's own /close) and recommends deleting it. The B19 ruling names copies of retired suite verbs and the project's files inside them; it names no user whose same-named skill the suite never wrote. Scope: caused by the change (RETIRED_VENDORED additions, admin/converge lines 125-130).

Changed definition: admin/converge::expected()/owned()/FIXED_RULES/MODULE_MARKER now materialize, as suite-owned and overwritten on converge, two fixed-content files with no stamp (.claude/rules/ok-concepts.md, .ok-planner/package.json) and, taken over from the retired plumbline and front-door cores, rules files and hooks stamped on line 2 or 3 (plumbline-cheatsheet.md, plumbline-coding.md, ok-cheatsheet.md, .claude/hooks/ok-agent-model, ok-subagent-batching). User: the triage prompt's suite-owned test, triage.md line 19: "A file is suite-owned when /ok overwrites it on every converge: its last line is a `Materialized by ok-` stamp, or it lies under .ok-planner/review/catalog/", restated in ok-planner-cheatsheet.md lines 129-131. Goal (triage.md and the cheatsheet's Defect issues section): a change to a file /ok overwrites goes upstream to the ok-plugins suite, never to the project's /plan-sprint. Trigger: an issue asking to change .claude/rules/ok-concepts.md or .ok-planner/package.json (no stamp at all), or a head-stamped rules file or hook. Old outcome for the two fixed-content files: they did not exist. New outcome: the test reads them as project-owned, triage routes the change to /plan-sprint, and the next /ok finds the edited file no longer matches its fixed bytes and offers it as a collision to delete, undoing the project's change. Scope: caused for the two fixed-content files added by WI1 and WI14; the head-stamped rules files stood at the base under the same test, and are now planner files the planner's own definition misses.

decision:project-chooses-its-lint-checks: 'Turning a check off also drops its rule from the suite-owned rules text the project's agents read, so the written rule and the lint never disagree'; decision:tests-forbidden (amended this sprint): 'A project may turn the test check off; the rule then drops from the rules text its agents read'. Code site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md:34 (## Scope) keeps the no-tests rule outside any '<!-- lint-check: no-tests -->' block: 'Nothing here adds, edits, runs, or reads a test.' admin/converge::render_rules drops only marked blocks, so in a project whose .ok-planner/config.json sets lint_checks.no-tests false, the vendored .claude/skills/converge/SKILL.md still tells every /converge session that nothing adds, edits, runs, or reads a test, while fix.md, verify.md, and backout.md (marked by WI6) drop the same rule: the rule text and the lint disagree, and the converge skill disagrees with its own prompts. Every other unconditional test or comment rule in the payload's skills, rules templates, and docs was searched (rg 'no test|edit no test|tests' over skills/, scripts/*.md, docs/, review/catalog/, agents/); this is the one unmarked site. Scope: caused — the line stood at the base, but WI6 introduced the switch and the commitment, and the change marked its sibling prompts and not this sentence.

Entry A3 (an operator action through a shipped script crashes and leaves the product half-settled). Trigger: the owner accepts the worktrees:<dir> offer (bash admin/converge resolve worktrees:...) while a listed wt/* branch is checked out in the main worktree (merged into HEAD trivially), or while a listed worktree is locked or holds a submodule. Path: admin/converge resolve -> worktree_refusals(o) -> loop 'subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, "worktree", "remove", tree], check=True)' / 'subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, "branch", "-d", branch], check=True)'. worktree_refusals builds 'elsewhere' from registered_worktrees(), which returns trees[1:] and so never sees the main worktree, and it checks no lock; the refusal passes, git refuses ('Cannot delete branch ... checked out at', or 'worktree is locked'), and check=True raises an uncaught CalledProcessError: the operator gets a Python traceback, and the worktrees removed earlier in the loop stay removed while the rest of the set and every branch remain. The core's own contract is a named refusal that changes nothing ('resolve refuses, changing nothing, unless...'). Scope: caused — the worktrees offer and its resolve are new in this change.

Converge removes a committed .ok-workspaces/config.json (the workspaces profile) by git rm with no cleanup offer, even where the owner hand-edited it and added keys of their own (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/converge:workspaces_plan); the plumbline migration offers any file it does not recognize as estate-leftover. One reading: the profile is the suite's retired-layout content, which decision whole-file-ownership lets converge migrate mechanically, and the sprint's notes rule it removed by git rm, recoverable from history. The other reading: story converge-project-estate promises upgrading never costs work the owner wrote, and work item 3 says owner content arrives unchanged, so a hand-edited profile is owner-declared configuration and owes an offer (estate-leftover or estate-edits) before removal. From failure i25.

port-block reads a record entry's port from its file and prints it with exit 0 even when the dev server that wrote it has stopped (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/port-block:recorded_port), while a service entry refuses when no container of the service runs. The OS may hand that freed port to another run's server, so a run that reads it back could verify against the other run's stack. One reading: decision os-assigned-ports-read-back-by-run-tag promises only a readback of the port the stack got, and clearing a stale record is the project's stack commands' job. The other reading: the story promises one verification run never disturbs another's results, so port-block owes a refusal for a record port nothing listens on, matching the service branch. From failure i28.

body: In a scratch consumer project (converge core, then git commit as base): wrote a minimal sprint at .ok-planner/sprints/2026-10-04-certify-completion-873314a4.md with a work item, implementation notes, a completion contract, and a closing /converge sprint line. Added src/app.py. Ran review changed --sprint S, which printed 'added src/app.py'. Ran tasks init, then review checks --base HEAD --sprint S, which filed exec t1 'node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline src/app.py'. Ran tasks next and tasks exec t1, which printed 'closed t1 done (exit 0)'. Ran review prompt --name sprint-review, which wrote the review agent's prompt. Committed the work, then ran review changed --sprint S again with no --base: it printed nothing and exited 0. The same happened with a recorded base file beside the sprint under the names <sprint>-base, <sprint>-base.txt, and <sprint>.base: none was honoured. Only an explicit --base HEAD~1 listed the change again ('added src/app.py'). The story promises: the owner knows, when a sprint closes, whether what they approved was delivered, the same way for every sprint. Saw: the command line runs the mechanical steps but gives no verdict on delivery. review --help and every subcommand's --help print bare usage with no description of what a step does, so an owner cannot tell from the command line which steps make a certification. review changed --sprint without --base falls back silently to HEAD. After the sprint's work is committed, that fallback reports an empty change with exit 0 and no warning that no base was recorded, so a review fed from it would see nothing to judge. Evidence: '== changed --sprint (no base file, work committed)' followed by no output and 'exit 0'; 'review changed --base HEAD~1 --sprint S' prints 'added src/app.py'; 'review changed --help' prints only 'usage: review changed [-h] [--base BASE] [--sprint SPRINT]'.
note: the driver expected the review CLI to give a delivery verdict and to honour the sprint's recorded base under 'review changed --sprint'; story certify-completion is offered through /converge sprint, which reads the -base.txt file and passes --base itself, and review changed's --base default of HEAD stands the same at the base commit. No message the user met misstated an error; what the driver lacked was a CLI step that reads the recorded base and a described help text: question i75.

body: With citation tags declared (converge resolve citation-tags), a file whose line 1 is '#!/usr/bin/env python3' and line 2 is '# @story: greet-by-name' (the slug resolves) fails the lint: 'plumbline/comment-hygiene: citation comment must be slug-only — each line is `@<tag>: <slug>` and nothing else'. The same line with no shebang above it passes (exit 0), with or without a .py extension tested. The cheatsheet allows a shebang as a machine directive and a slug-only citation line; together they are refused, and the message names the wrong cause. Every executable script that cites the corpus on line 2 is blocked. evidence: probe files bin/probe2 (no extension) and bin/probe3.py both exit 2 with that message; bin/p1.py with the citation on line 1 exits 0.
note: site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/plumbline:checkCommentHygiene (mergeConsecutiveLineComments folds a line-1 shebang into the citation comment below it, so isPureCitationBlock fails); entry A3 (the lint, a script project.md lists, refuses a shebang plus a slug-only citation the cheatsheet allows, with a message naming the wrong cause); evidence: '#!/usr/bin/env python3' then '# @story: greet' gives 'p.py:2: plumbline/comment-hygiene: citation comment must be slug-only' exit 2, and the citation alone passes; outside the sprint: the base commit's lint (plugins/ok/families/ok-plumbline/bin/plumbline) gives the identical violation on the same file, and the sprint moved the lint without changing its comment grouping.

(line 882) and 'usage: converge resolve <id> [<choice>|--from <draft>]' (line 2351). body: In a scratch consumer project (mktemp -d, git init) I ran the converge core with no mode, then 'converge wire-hooks lint' (wired: ok-planner lint entries transcribed into .claude/settings.json (PostToolUse)). In a real Claude Code session (claude -p --model haiku --permission-mode acceptEdits) an agent Write of src/greet.py with the line '    # build the greeting string for the user' was blocked ('PostToolUse:Write hook blocking error ... src/greet.py:2: plumbline/comment-hygiene: comment is not permitted'). I committed the file, then a second session used Edit to insert '    # prefix the name with a friendly hi' directly below the existing comment line. The hook did not block: the agent reported 'NO HOOK FEEDBACK.' and git diff -U0 shows '@@ -2,0 +3 @@ +    # prefix the name with a friendly hi'. Feeding the hook directly gives the same: a PostToolUse Edit or Write payload for that file exits 0, while a new comment in a separate spot of the same file (line 8) exits 2. node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline src/greet.py reports only 'src/greet.py:2: plumbline/comment-hygiene' and nothing for line 3, so the hook appears to keep only violations whose reported line is changed, and a new comment line appended to an existing comment block is reported at the block's unchanged first line and dropped; the story promises: every agent edit is checked as it lands, so that residue never accumulates; saw: a new prose comment line written by an agent Edit landed with no block and no feedback, and the whole-file lint folds it into the old block's report; evidence: hook exit=0 on the Edit payload, session result 'NO HOOK FEEDBACK.', diff '+    # prefix the name with a friendly hi' at line 3 of src/greet.py

- i58: B6 ruling: 'migrate: the /ok report names the new rules and the lint_checks switch, the hook stays behind consent, and without node nothing is wired'. plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md:7. Report: the template names the version row, wiring, offers, migrations, and removed verbs; lint_checks appears only in the retired-verb row '| budget | retired; turn a lint check off with lint_checks |' (SKILL.md:96), printed only where a /budget skill was removed. ADMINISTRATION.md carries no instruction to report the new rules or the switch. Trigger: /ok on a project that ran ok-planner alone. Harm (R2): the planner-only owner gains plumbline-cheatsheet.md, plumbline-coding.md and the lint, and the report tells them neither that the rules now bind nor how to turn checks off, contrary to the migrate ruling. Reports: i34.
- i59: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/converge:retirements and the retired-verb offer. RETIRED_VENDORED (converge:125-130) now adds generic names: 'slug', 'ci', 'budget', 'events', 'explain', 'patterns', 'port', 'starter', 'suggest', 'version', 'open', 'close', 'ok-workspaces', 'ok-planner', 'execute-tasks'; retirements() treats a folder whose SKILL.md has no suite stamp as 'the project's own whole' (converge:987-988 'out.append((name, [], files))'), and the offer (converge:1866-1873) says '.claude/skills/<name>/ holds files the project wrote at a name the suite retired; the vendored skills replace it' with 'Recommended: accept' (converge:2009 default) and a fix that deletes every file. Trigger: /ok on a project the suite never vendored that verb into (e.g. planner-only at the base) that keeps its own skill at .claude/skills/close/, open/, version/, ci/, events/ or port/. Before (base RETIRED_VENDORED held only suite-specific names, converge@9c7aff7:262-263): left alone. After: reported as a retired suite verb the vendored skills replace, recommended for deletion. Harm (R5): a boundary user (Converged projects) whose same-named skill the suite never wrote; B19/B21/B28/B29/B118 rule the removal of retired suite verbs and name no such user. Reports: i35.
- i63: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/converge:worktree_refusals and resolve's worktrees branch. worktree_refusals (converge:1445-1458) builds 'elsewhere' from registered_worktrees(), which returns 'trees[1:]' (converge:1392) and so never sees the main worktree's branch, and it checks no lock. resolve (converge:2419-2428) then runs 'subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, "worktree", "remove", tree], check=True)' and 'subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, "branch", "-d", branch], check=True)'. Trigger: the owner accepts the worktrees: offer while a listed wt/* branch is checked out in the main worktree (merged into HEAD trivially) or a listed worktree is locked. Harm (A3): git refuses, CalledProcessError escapes as a traceback, and the worktrees removed earlier in the loop stay removed while the rest and every branch remain, against the core's contract that resolve refuses changing nothing. Reports: i45.
- i71: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/converge, the top-level mode dispatch (MODE="converge"; case "${1:-}" in diagnose|wire-hooks|wire-env|resolve ... esac, lines 8-14). What the code does: any first argument that names no mode, a help request included (--help, -h, help, --version, a typo such as bogus or nonsense-mode), leaves MODE at converge, and the script runs the full converge against the project at the working directory and exits 0. Trigger: an operator runs 'converge --help' (or mistypes a mode) to learn the core's modes, a script project.md lists for developers and operators. Harm (A3): the action gives a wrong result with no message saying what the user did wrong; it performs the one deliberate act story converge-project-estate reserves to the owner: it materializes 74 files, moves owner config (.ok-plumbline/config.json -> .ok-planner/config.json), git rm's retired estates (staged), deletes retired skills and agent profiles, and rewrites live sprint files. Plumbline-coding rule 4.8 decides the fix form: a value an end user supplies is checked where it enters and refused with a message the user can act on; the sibling refusals in the same core are 'usage: converge wire-hooks <group>, where <group> is one of: ...' (line 882) and 'usage: converge resolve <id> [<choice>|--from <draft>]' (line 2351). Scope: the sprint rewrote this dispatch (added wire-env, B4's group argument) and made the default mode migrate and git rm retired estates, so a mistaken argument now reaches that migration. Evidence: drivers quote 'materialized: 74 files under .ok-planner/ and .claude/ (v23.0.0)' and 'Converged ok-planner at /Users/patrick/Documents/projects/research/ok-plugins (already present; CLAUDE.md written from template, v23.0.0).' exit 0 for --help; 'converge bogus' in a scratch repo exits 0 the same way; at the monorepo root '--help' printed 'moved: .ok-plumbline/config.json -> .ok-planner/config.json' and 'removed: .ok-plumbline/LICENSE (git rm; staged)'. Failures: i17, i20, i22, i24, i29, i30.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/converge:retirements and the retired-verb offer. RETIRED_VENDORED (converge:125-130) now adds generic names: 'slug', 'ci', 'budget', 'events', 'explain', 'patterns', 'port', 'starter', 'suggest', 'version', 'open', 'close', 'ok-workspaces', 'ok-planner', 'execute-tasks'; retirements() treats a folder whose SKILL.md has no suite stamp as 'the project's own whole' (converge:987-988 'out.append((name, [], files))'), and the offer (converge:1866-1873) says '.claude/skills/<name>/ holds files the project wrote at a name the suite retired; the vendored skills replace it' with 'Recommended: accept' (converge:2009 default) and a fix that deletes every file. Trigger: /ok on a project the suite never vendored that verb into (e.g. planner-only at the base) that keeps its own skill at .claude/skills/close/, open/, version/, ci/, events/ or port/. Before (base RETIRED_VENDORED held only suite-specific names, converge@9c7aff7:262-263): left alone. After: reported as a retired suite verb the vendored skills replace, recommended for deletion. Harm (R5): a boundary user (Converged projects) whose same-named skill the suite never wrote; B19/B21/B28/B29/B118 rule the removal of retired suite verbs and name no such user. Reports: i35.
note: converge: the generic names the consolidation retired (slug, ci, budget, events, explain, patterns, port, starter, suggest, version, open, close, ok-workspaces, ok-planner, execute-tasks) move from RETIRED_VENDORED to a new RETIRED_WHERE_STAMPED tuple. retirements() still removes their suite-stamped files and offers project files beside them, and offers the leftovers once converge has removed the suite's SKILL.md; a folder holding an unstamped SKILL.md at one of those names is a project skill the suite never wrote and is left alone (base behavior). Base and ok-core names keep the whole-folder offer. ADMINISTRATION.md's retired-verb row and section say so. Verified in a scratch repo: an unstamped .claude/skills/close/ is not offered, plan-sprint-code still is, and a stamped close/ with a project file has its stamped file removed and the project file offered. Files: admin/converge, admin/ADMINISTRATION.md.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/converge:worktree_refusals and resolve's worktrees branch. worktree_refusals (converge:1445-1458) builds 'elsewhere' from registered_worktrees(), which returns 'trees[1:]' (converge:1392) and so never sees the main worktree's branch, and it checks no lock. resolve (converge:2419-2428) then runs 'subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, "worktree", "remove", tree], check=True)' and 'subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, "branch", "-d", branch], check=True)'. Trigger: the owner accepts the worktrees: offer while a listed wt/* branch is checked out in the main worktree (merged into HEAD trivially) or a listed worktree is locked. Harm (A3): git refuses, CalledProcessError escapes as a traceback, and the worktrees removed earlier in the loop stay removed while the rest and every branch remain, against the core's contract that resolve refuses changing nothing. Reports: i45.
note: converge: registered_worktrees() now returns every worktree, the main one included, with a locked flag from the porcelain 'locked' line; workspaces_plan slices [1:] as before. worktree_refusals refuses a listed worktree that is locked or holds populated submodules (gitdir/modules or a .gitmodules path with a .git), and builds 'elsewhere' from all worktrees, so a wt/* branch checked out in the main worktree is refused. Those are the git worktree remove / branch -d refusals the loop could hit after clean+merged checks, so resolve now refuses before changing anything. Refusal suffix now 'Settle each one'; the offer's fix text and both ADMINISTRATION.md passages name the new conditions. Verified in a scratch repo: locked, main-checkout and submodule cases refused with nothing changed; the cleared case removes all. Files: admin/converge, admin/ADMINISTRATION.md.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/converge, the top-level mode dispatch (MODE="converge"; case "${1:-}" in diagnose|wire-hooks|wire-env|resolve ... esac, lines 8-14). What the code does: any first argument that names no mode, a help request included (--help, -h, help, --version, a typo such as bogus or nonsense-mode), leaves MODE at converge, and the script runs the full converge against the project at the working directory and exits 0. Trigger: an operator runs 'converge --help' (or mistypes a mode) to learn the core's modes, a script project.md lists for developers and operators. Harm (A3): the action gives a wrong result with no message saying what the user did wrong; it performs the one deliberate act story converge-project-estate reserves to the owner: it materializes 74 files, moves owner config (.ok-plumbline/config.json -> .ok-planner/config.json), git rm's retired estates (staged), deletes retired skills and agent profiles, and rewrites live sprint files. Plumbline-coding rule 4.8 decides the fix form: a value an end user supplies is checked where it enters and refused with a message the user can act on; the sibling refusals in the same core are 'usage: converge wire-hooks <group>, where <group> is one of: ...' (line 882) and 'usage: converge resolve <id> [<choice>|--from <draft>]' (line 2351). Scope: the sprint rewrote this dispatch (added wire-env, B4's group argument) and made the default mode migrate and git rm retired estates, so a mistaken argument now reaches that migration. Evidence: drivers quote 'materialized: 74 files under .ok-planner/ and .claude/ (v23.0.0)' and 'Converged ok-planner at /Users/patrick/Documents/projects/research/ok-plugins (already present; CLAUDE.md written from template, v23.0.0).' exit 0 for --help; 'converge bogus' in a scratch repo exits 0 the same way; at the monorepo root '--help' printed 'moved: .ok-plumbline/config.json -> .ok-planner/config.json' and 'removed: .ok-plumbline/LICENSE (git rm; staged)'. Failures: i17, i20, i22, i24, i29, i30.
note: converge's top-level dispatch now converges only with no argument; diagnose|wire-hooks|wire-env|resolve select their mode; -h/--help/help print the usage line and exit 0; any other first argument (an empty one included) prints 'converge: <arg> names no mode; nothing written' plus the usage line to stderr and exits 1 before resolving the root or writing anything, per coding rule 4.8. Placeholders are upper case (GROUP, ID) because checks/owned-paths reads '>' in a bash line as a redirect. ADMINISTRATION.md's modes section says so. Verified: --help and 'nonsense' in a scratch repo write nothing. Files: admin/converge, admin/ADMINISTRATION.md.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/converge, the top-level mode dispatch (MODE="converge"; case "${1:-}" in diagnose|wire-hooks|wire-env|resolve ... esac, lines 8-14). What the code does: any first argument that names no mode, a help request included (--help, -h, help, --version, a typo such as bogus or nonsense-mode), leaves MODE at converge, and the script runs the full converge against the project at the working directory and exits 0. Trigger: an operator runs 'converge --help' (or mistypes a mode) to learn the core's modes, a script project.md lists for developers and operators. Harm (A3): the action gives a wrong result with no message saying what the user did wrong; it performs the one deliberate act story converge-project-estate reserves to the owner: it materializes 74 files, moves owner config (.ok-plumbline/config.json -> .ok-planner/config.json), git rm's retired estates (staged), deletes retired skills and agent profiles, and rewrites live sprint files. (line 882) and 'usage: converge resolve <id> [<choice>|--from <draft>]' (line 2351). The other reading: story converge-project-estate promises upgrading never costs work the owner wrote, and work item 3 says owner content arrives unchanged, so a hand-edited profile is owner-declared configuration and owes an offer (estate-leftover or estate-edits) before removal. body: port-block reads a record entry's port from its file and prints it with exit 0 even when the dev server that wrote it has stopped (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/port-block:recorded_port), while a service entry refuses when no container of the service runs. The OS may hand that freed port to another run's server, so a run that reads it back could verify against the other run's stack. One reading: decision os-assigned-ports-read-back-by-run-tag promises only a readback of the port the stack got, and clearing a stale record is the project's stack commands' job. The other reading: the story promises one verification run never disturbs another's results, so port-block owes a refusal for a record port nothing listens on, matching the service branch. From failure i28.

One reading: the review CLI is the orchestrator's mechanics and owes nothing beyond its usage line. The other reading: the CLI is a script project.md lists for developers and operators, so 'review changed --sprint' owes the sprint's recorded base, or a warning that it fell back to HEAD, and its help owes a description of the certification steps. From failure i19.

body: decision:generated-catalog-tocs (amended this sprint, which also dropped the audit and certification backstop sentence) says 'a generator writes that file from the catalog's own artifacts' for every durable catalog. The payload's one generator script, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/catalog-toc (materialized as .ok-planner/bin/catalog-toc), regenerates only subjects.md and practices.md (CATALOGS lists those two); the design TOCs concepts.md, stories.md, decisions.md are written by an agent following discover-design step 7 or the sprint build prompt, by hand each time. Reading A: an agent following a fixed procedure is 'a generator', and the code complies. Reading B: the decision means a mechanical generator, so catalog-toc should also cover the three design catalogs, or the decision should say the design TOCs are agent-written. After the sprint's work is committed, that fallback reports an empty change with exit 0 and no warning that no base was recorded, so a review fed from it would see nothing to judge. Evidence: '== changed --sprint (no base file, work committed)' followed by no output and 'exit 0'; 'review changed --base HEAD~1 --sprint S' prints 'added src/app.py'; 'review changed --help' prints only 'usage: review changed [-h] [--base BASE] [--sprint SPRINT]'.
